=== History ===
According to the “Kamo Daimyōjin Denki” (1742), during the “Tenpyō era” of {{ill|Empress Kōken|Q232955|qid=Q232955}}{{efn|However, the era names during Empress Kōken’s reign were {{ill|Tenpyō-shōhō|Q1373169|qid=Q1373169}} and {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|qid=Q1346307}}, while {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} was an era of the reign of {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263|lt=Shōmu}}.}}, Tamayasu-hime-no-Mikoto visited Kamo-ura in Oki Province and established the shrine{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}.

It is an ancient shrine listed in the “{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}” as “Kamonabi Shrine”{{efn|In the Yoshida family manuscript it appears as “Kamonamibi Shrine”{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}.}}{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}.

In the early modern period it was known as “Kamo Daimyōjin”{{efn|“Inshū Shichō Gōki” (1667){{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}.}}, “Kamo Daimyōjin”{{efn|“Inshūki” (1688), “Tōgo Kyūsha Torishirabechō” (1871), etc.{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}.}}, and in the “{{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|Q11420490|qid=Q11420490|lt=Inshū Jinmyōchō}}” it is listed as “Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Kamo Nabi Myōjin”{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}{{efn|This “Junior Fourth Rank Upper” is said to derive from a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōgen Senji}}{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}. It has also been noted that compared to other shrines within Oki Province, this rank is low despite being a Shikinai shrine{{sfn|Rikahinosha|1987b|p=290}}.}}. Since the Meiji period, it has reverted to the old name from the Engishiki and has been called “Kamonabi Shrine”{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
=== Principal deity ===
* '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakeikazuchi-no-Kami}}''' (わけいかづちのかみ)
: The enshrined deity of {{ill|Kamigamo Shrine|Q700448|qid=Q700448}}, and this shrine is regarded as a {{ill|Bunrei|es|Bunrei|fr|Bunrei|id|Bunrei|ja|分霊|simple|Bunrei|qid=Q195793}} of Kamo Wakeikazuchi Shrine{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=965}}. Among the Shikinai shrines of Oki Province, this shrine alone is a shrine of a transferred deity, leading to a theory that from the medieval period onward, a {{ill|Wandering miko|Q11546650|qid=Q11546650}} (the model for Tamayasu-hime-no-Mikoto mentioned below) promoted the idea that “Kamonabi is the Kamo deity,” and thus Wakeikazuchi-no-Kami came to be enshrined here{{sfn|Rikahinosha|1987b|pp=289–290}}.
: This deity was originally enshrined in Kyoto, but in seeking to cultivate new lands, shot an arrow adorned with leaves of the {{ill|Malvaceae|Q156551|qid=Q156551|lt=Aoi}} plant, deciding to travel to where the arrow landed{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|p=74}}. Following the arrow’s trajectory, the deity departed by boat from {{ill|Wakasa Bay|Q11616636|qid=Q11616636}} and arrived at the Oki Islands{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|pp=74–75}}. The place where the arrow struck came to be called “Mato no Mae,” and a rock bearing the shape of a target can still be seen today{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|p=75}}. The deity moored at “Funashima” and visited the Kamo settlement{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|p=75}}, teaching the people weaving, fishing, shipbuilding, agriculture, and providing medical care{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|pp=76–78}}. The people wished to repay the deity, and Kaede-hime, the most beautiful woman in the village, hoped to become the deity’s consort{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|pp=78–79}}. The deity accepted her, and together they devoted themselves to helping the villagers{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|pp=79–80}}. As a renewed expression of gratitude, the villagers built a large palace{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|p=81}}. This is said to be the origin of the shrine; afterward, although the deity passed away, the soul is believed to still be enshrined here{{sfn|Yokoyama|1966|p=81}}. Such legends are preserved.

=== Associated deities ===
* '''{{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}''' (すさのおのみこと)
* '''Tamayasu-hime-no-Mikoto''' (たまやすひめのみこと)
: As mentioned above, she is a deity with characteristics similar to a walking miko who is said to have come to the island during Empress Kōken’s reign; her place of origin is unknown{{sfn|Rikahinosha|1987a|p=185}}.

=== Structures ===
[[File:Kamonabi Shrine Honden.jpg|thumb|Main hall of Kamonabi Shrine]]
; Main hall
: Three bays wide (3.96 meters), two bays deep (3.17 meters), with a ridge height of approximately 8 meters from the ground{{sfn|Okinoshima Town Board of Education}}. Built in the {{ill|Oki-zukuri|Q11659055|qid=Q11659055}} style with a copper roof{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}, it features a karahafu gable at the center of the front porch{{sfn|Okinoshima Town Board of Education}}. Constructed in Bunsei 11 (1828), it has been designated a town cultural property as described below{{sfn|Okinoshima Town Board of Education}}.
; Connecting hall
: Copper-roofed {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}}, with a floor area of 4 tsubo. Built in 1918 (Taishō 7){{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Worship hall
: Copper-roofed {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}, with a floor area of 16 tsubo. Built in 1918 (Taishō 7){{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Treasure storehouse{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}
; Lodging for worshippers{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}
: In Oki, after praying at one’s tutelary shrine for recovery from illness, safe childbirth, a good catch, school admission, and the like, there was a custom called “Okomori,” in which one would spend the night in a hut within the shrine grounds called a “Komosha” or “Komoriya” as thanks for the fulfillment of the prayer{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=310}}.
; Torii
: A wooden Myōjin-style torii{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Stone lanterns
: Four lanterns as of 1983{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.

=== Festivals ===
; Grand festival
: According to the early Meiji-era “Tōgo Shrine Investigation Register,” held on the first or middle Rooster Day of April{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}. Since the adoption of the solar calendar, the annual festival has been called the “Aoi Festival” and is held on April 21{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Minor festivals
: According to the “Tōgo Shrine Investigation Register,” held on the 1st, 11th, and 21st of each month{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; New Year festival
: January 7{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Hyakute Festival
: March 11{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}. Three boys whose parents are both alive shoot bows{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Gion Festival
: June 15{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Gozaide Festival
: September 30{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}. A festival marking the shrine’s deity departing for Izumo during {{ill|Kannazuki|Q6364021|qid=Q6364021|lt=the time when the gods gather in Izumo}}{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
; Gozairi Festival
: October 30{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}. A festival marking the shrine’s deity returning from Izumo{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=966}}.
